FRA: France emerged from the First World War facing reconstruction and security concerns. Its industry, overseas interests and scientific institutions offered several paths to national development. This scenario uses modern borders and fictional starting resources.
DEU: Germany entered the 1920s under the Weimar Republic, with extensive industrial skills amid political and economic instability. This alternate-history campaign lets you choose an industrial, scientific or military direction. Modern borders are used.
GBR: Britain entered the interwar period with a large maritime network and an economy adjusting after the First World War. Naval logistics, aviation and research provide natural strategic options. This scenario uses modern borders.
USA: The United States entered the 1920s with an expanding industrial economy and growing technological capabilities. Its geographic scale supports a production-led strategy. Starting resources are fictional and borders are modern.
CHN: China's 1920s were shaped by fragmented political authority and efforts toward national consolidation. This scenario treats the modern map as a single playable command for an alternate industrial history.
RUS: The lands represented by modern Russia entered the 1920s after revolution and civil war. Rebuilding transport and industry provides a foundation for this alternate-history scenario, which uses modern boundaries.
JPN: Japan entered the interwar period with substantial manufacturing capacity and growing naval and industrial ambitions. As an island nation, maritime logistics are central to this scenario. Modern borders and fictional resources are used.
IND: The lands represented by modern India were under British colonial rule in 1920. This alternate-history scenario instead begins with an independent playable command, emphasizing industrial development and research. Modern borders are used.
